THE RED, WHITE & BLUE STORY
Al Hirt is one of the most popular and talented
trumpet players of our time. Because of the many demands
for his personal appearance he is a frequent air traveler,
and United is his favorite airline.
When United recently introduced its Red, White & Blue
transcontinental service, Al was among the first to try it.
As with almost every other person who has traveled
Red. White & Blue, he liked it.
In fact, Al was so pleased with the new service that
United asked him to set his enthusiasm to music. He readily
agreed, and the result is his own composition, "Red, Whit &
Blue." It's a happy and pleasant tune. We like it, Al like it,
and we believe you will like it too.

The ultimate in luxury travel. Spacious two-and-two seating. Six-course gourmet

STANDARD
This is the exclusive extra choice United offers you, comparable to our One-Class

seating. Delicious four-course meal and your choice of complimentary beverages.
Priced between First Class and Coach.
COACH
Our special combination of excellent food, complimentary beverage, and gracious

fare across the U.S.

THE
HIGH-FLYING
TRUMPET OF
AL HIRT
About the only thing with which one can compare
Al Hirt's dynamism as a performer is the drama of
his arrival on the scene as the country's most popu-
lar trumpeter. It was an occasion long in the making,
but sudden and sure in its impact. Where most
modern-day Gabriels have sprung almost solely from
the conservatory, the dance band or jazz, Al bring:
to the market place a bushel of experience in all *
three, a preparation for stardom that involves twenty
years of incomparable knowledge and skill.
As surely as "Honey in the Horn" marks the turn-
ing point in Al Hirt's career, it is the combination of
experience factors that accounts for his appeal to
every conceivable type of listener. Mood music,
Dixieland, popular ballads and novelty songs all bear
the stamp of his brash but highly melodic style;
there is, indeed, scarcely anybody's musical cup of
tea that is not warmed and stirred by his perform-
ing. With this in mind, the present sampling of
diverse recordings by "The King" was made.
"The High-Flying Trumpet" lifts off with an origi-
nal salute, Red, White & Blue, followed by a haunt-
ing guitar-powered treatment of Walkin', one of the
instrumental "sleeper" hits of our time. Dear Old
Southland is an amalgam, too seldom played, of
Deep River and other traditional material created
by the team of Henry Creamer and Turner Layton
who also, appropriately, gave the world Way Down
Yonder in New Orleans. Victor Young's ever-popular
Sweet-Sue is in fact flanked by tradition,
since
traces of the melody to Down by the Riverside have
been located as early as the vear 1861.
Side 2 opens 103 years later, so to speak, with the
peerless smash title song to Broadway's current
favorite "Hello, Dollv!" Its unique blend of horn
and voices is followed by a true piece of homage
to the instrument and to one of its greatest ex-
ponents, Bunny Berigan-I Can't Get Started. For
sheer virtuositv. Al next selects two particularly
contrasting numbers: Muskrat Ramble, a national
anthem of Dixieland, and Out of Nowhere, a verita-
ble rhapsody for trumpet and strings. A companion
piece to Southland is provided in Talkin' 'bout That
River, a doff to the traditional by the singing great,
Ray Charles.

RED, WHITE & BLUE
Al Hirt composed and recorded Red, White
& Blue especially for United Air Lines as a
theme for its Extra Care service. Svmbolic of
the company's official colors, Red, White &
Blue expresses the speed and modernity of
United's great jet fleet and the scope of its
far-flung route system covering the entire
nation.
